extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing manuscripts for the Bulletin of Symbolic Logic (mathematical logic community)
extracted.subtask_description: Author instructions for preparing and submitting manuscripts (Articles, Communications, Thesis Abstracts, Reviews) to the Bulletin of Symbolic Logic, including formatting, accessibility, prior-publication policy, and supplementary-materials guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article: scope and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles present topics of broad interest in a way that is accessible to a large audience. They can be purely expository, survey, or historical articles or they may contain, in addition, new ideas or results or new approaches to old ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers should aim to be accessible to a wide audience within the field; may combine exposition with new results or approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication: purpose and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications should be announcements of important new results and ideas in any aspect of logic; they may be short papers in their final form or preliminary announcements (extended abstracts, position papers) of longer, full papers that will be published elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should include, in addition to a description of the new results or ideas, enough history, background, and explanation to make the significance of the work apparent to a wide audience. Communications will be quickly refereed and published within six months of receipt of the final versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable non-standard submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Other high quality submissions not exactly in the Articles/Communications categories may be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions should be sent to the Managing Editor for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format: initial and post-acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be submitted in PDF. After acceptance a LaTeX source file, preferably using the asl document class (asl.cls) and BibTeX style (asl.bst), and a pdf produced from the source are requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of asl.cls and asl.bst is preferred; submission handled via the partner submission system (account required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and prior-publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The BSL publishes only original papers that have not been published previously, and are not submitted for publication elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full versions of important papers previously published in conference proceedings are eligible provided the submitted paper extends the pre-publication in a significant way; authors must provide a precise reference to the pre-publication and explain the extent to which the submission differs from the conference version. Deposition of a preprint on a personal website, in an institutional repository, or in a preprint archive shall not be viewed as prior or duplicate publication. Authors should follow the Cambridge University Press Preprint Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis abstracts: eligibility and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Thesis abstracts will be accepted for students who received the Ph.D. in the past three years and are to be submitted by the thesis advisor (for a student with two advisors, either one may submit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is hoped to publish abstracts for all recent Ph.D. theses in logic; advisors are expected to request their former students to do the actual writing when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis abstracts: required heading information
rubrics_metrics.description: The heading for a thesis abstract should give: Author of thesis; Title of thesis; University or other institution granting degree; Year in which Ph.D. was conferred; Thesis advisor(s); MSC classification: at least one primary and up to two secondary; url for thesis (optional); Keywords (optional); email address for author (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided Template for Thesis Abstracts and style file; abstracts should be prepared in TeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis abstracts: length and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The body of the abstract should briefly say what is in the thesis; the suggested length is one page, and two pages is the absolute upper bound. Abstracts should be in English and prepared in TeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission should indicate whether it was taken directly from the thesis, and, if not, whether it was prepared solely by the student, solely by the advisor, or by the advisor and student in collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: English language editing (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors, particularly those whose first language is not English, may wish to have their English-language manuscripts checked by a native speaker before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cambridge offers language-editing services which are voluntary and at the author's own expense. Use of these services does not guarantee acceptance nor restrict submission to other Cambridge journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID encouragement and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to identify themselves using ORCID when submitting a manuscript to this journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits listed include discoverability, convenience, and keeping track of research activities. ORCID 'Published Name' field may be used to indicate pronouns/titles; ORCID use is optional and not currently recommended for author name changes (see the author name change policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility requirements (WCAG)
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles published by Cambridge are required to meet the accessibility standards outlined in the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider elements such as colour use, contrast, and text clarity when preparing images and tables. See the Cambridge Journals Artwork Guide for detailed guidance on image and multimedia file preparation and preferred formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image, table, and multimedia descriptions (alt-text)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessibility materials must be made available for all figures, tables, and multimedia content to be published within the article, including the provision of image descriptions or 'alt-text' for all figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged, as subject experts, to prepare their own accessibility materials and submit them via the Accessibility Descriptions Submission Form. If not provided, these materials will be machine generated and made available to review at proof stage. The accuracy of accessibility materials is the responsibility of the author; ensure these are checked carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labelling and citation of illustrative materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All illustrative materials should be referred to in manuscript text as 'Figures'. Tables and figures must be cited in the text, must be numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals, and captions must be provided in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagrams, graphs, maps, boxes, graphical diagrams, and code snippets must also be labelled and numbered. Refer to 'Preparing Accessible Materials' for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials: scope and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Material that is not essential to understanding or supporting a manuscript, but which may be relevant or interesting to readers, may be submitted as supplementary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With editors' approval, supplementary material will be published online alongside the article but not in print pages. Types may include appendices, additional tables or figures, datasets, videos, and sound files. Supplementary materials will not be typeset or copyedited and should be supplied exactly as they are to appear online. Authors are encouraged to publish additional outputs in an appropriate repository and cite them in manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission logistics and system account
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript submissions are handled via a partner secure submission system for which authors need an account, separate from their Cambridge Core account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For login and submission support visit the submission and support pages. Authors should review the journal's author instructions (particularly 'preparing your materials') before submitting and use 'Proceed to submission system' to continue to the partner site.
